summary: Configured dnsmasq on node1 (Alpine 3.23) to resolve inventory-api.internal to node2's IP (10.100.231.11) while forwarding all other queries to the upstream resolver (10.100.231.1). Configured node2's /etc/resolv.conf to use node1 (10.100.231.10) as its DNS resolver, with dhcpcd's resolv.conf hook disabled (nohook resolv.conf) so the setting persists across DHCP renewals and reboots. Verified end-to-end resolution from node2 for both the internal name and external names. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node1 and node2 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed changed boot_id on each, and confirmed DNS service/config and resolution fully recovered post-restart on both nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected OS and existing DNS config on node1 and node2 (both Alpine 3.23.3)
Installed dnsmasq on node1 via apk
Wrote /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf on node1: listen on 127.0.0.1 and 10.100.231.10, address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.231.11, forward via server=10.100.231.1
Enabled and started dnsmasq service on node1 (rc-update add, rc-service start)
Verified node1 resolves inventory-api.internal to 10.100.231.11 and forwards external queries (google.com) correctly
Added 'nohook resolv.conf' to node2's /etc/dhcpcd.conf and set /etc/resolv.conf to 'nameserver 10.100.231.10'
Verified persistence of node2's resolv.conf across a dhcpcd service restart
Verified end-to-end resolution from node2: inventory-api.internal -> 10.100.231.11, plus external DNS still functional

Captured boot_id and service/DNS health baseline on node1, then rebooted node1 via 'reboot', polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id, and reverified dnsmasq status and DNS resolution

Captured boot_id and DNS config/resolution baseline on node2, then rebooted node2 via 'reboot', polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id, and reverified resolv.conf and DNS resolution

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal DNS resolver resolving inventory-api.internal to node2's IP
evidence.summary: dnsmasq installed and started on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.231.11; nslookup from node1 against 10.100.231.10 returns 10.100.231.11, and external queries (google.com) are still forwarded upstream correctly

evidence.requirement: node2 is configured to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups
evidence.summary: node2's /etc/resolv.conf set to nameserver 10.100.231.10 with dhcpcd resolv.conf hook disabled for persistence; verified it survives a dhcpcd restart; nslookup from node2 resolves inventory-api.internal to 10.100.231.11 and google.com resolves via node1 as well

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 87d66cb9... with dnsmasq healthy and resolving; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to db97d71d...; dnsmasq confirmed started and resolving both internal and external names post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6b98265c... with resolv.conf pointed at node1 and resolution working; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id changed to 503293e9...; resolv.conf persisted and DNS resolution (internal and external) confirmed working post-restart
